we characterized five OYEs from anaerobic bacteria that are involved in n‐naphthyl ring reductions.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the elucidation of the biochemical pathways of anaerobic n‐alkane degradation in sulfate‐reducing bacteria and with the identification of new OYEs involved in anaerobic degradation.
the identification and characterization of two OYEs involved in the ana‐erobic degradation of polycyclic aromatic compounds, which are important for the bioremediation of these compounds.
the identification and characterization of the first OYEs that reduce the naphthyl rings during anaerobic degradation.

NCRs are the first enzymes involved in naphthalene activation and the first enzymes that catalyze the reduction of a nonactivated aromatic ring.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the two‐step reduction of the naphthyl system is catalyzed by two OYEs, which is a novel and unexpected reaction for the OYE family.
two OYEs are involved in the anaerbic naphthyl reduction: one for the activation of the ring system (NCR) and another for the reduction of the activated naphthyl system (5,6DHNCR).

two distinct OYEs are involved in the ring reduction of NCoAs during anaerobic degradation: NCR catalyzes the two‐electron‐reduction to 5, 6‐DHN‐CoAs, and 5,6-DHN‐CoAs are further reduced by the 5,6-dihydro‐NCRs (5,6-DHNCRs) to the fully saturated THN‐CoA.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the OYE‐family members are versatile catalysts that are capable of reducing a wide range of compounds.
